nodes.name: src/spectre/jobs.rs
nodes.summary: Persistent job-tracker for spectre simulations: defines Job/JobStatus, persists them as JSON under the runtime cache, refreshes running jobs via local signal-0 / SSH kill -0 probes, cancels them by terminating the whole process group, and parses spectre.out to determine final status.

nodes.name: src/tui/app/action.rs
nodes.summary: Declares the Action enum (None, Quit, Refresh, CancelJob, SaveConfig, Status) emitted by the event handler and the handle_action dispatcher that mutates App state in response — keeping event-handling pure and pushing every data change through this funnel.

nodes.name: src/tui/app/data.rs
nodes.summary: Bridges the TUI App state and the rest of the CLI: loads session/job/tunnel lists, loads config.toml into editable ConfigField rows with VB_* env-override awareness, persists edited fields back to disk, and reads the command-log file for the log overlay.

nodes.name: src/tui/app/event.rs
nodes.summary: Terminal key-event cascade: routes keys with priority overlay → globals → tab content, drives vim-style nav (j/k, [/], Tab), opens the log/help/confirm/form overlays, and emits Action values; includes an emacs-style TextInput for the config form.

nodes.name: src/tui/app/mod.rs
nodes.summary: TUI app module root — re-exports the submodules and the two public entry points (handle_action, on_key) used by the event loop.

nodes.name: src/tui/app/overlay.rs
nodes.summary: Overlay state types: single-variant Overlay enum (None/Log/Confirm/Form/Help) plus a UTF-8-safe TextInput cursor for the form. Active overlay suppresses global keys via the event cascade.

nodes.name: src/tui/app/state.rs
nodes.summary: App state container — sessions/jobs/config-fields lists, per-tab selection cursors, status toast with 3s expiry, spinner frame, and tab cycling helpers (Sessions / Jobs / Config).

nodes.name: src/tui/mod.rs
nodes.summary: TUI binary entry point: sets raw mode + alternate screen, runs the draw/poll/key loop with a 500 ms poll that drives the spinner and daemon-stats refresh, and tears down the terminal cleanly on exit.

nodes.name: src/tui/theme.rs
nodes.summary: Color palette struct (primary/accent/success/error/warning/text/borders/surfaces) with NO_COLOR auto-detection and a builder override for the --no-color flag; all UI styling goes through Theme so accessibility mode is centralized.

nodes.name: src/tui/ui/chrome.rs
nodes.summary: Header chrome: bold title, tab chips (active/inactive), and right-aligned status badges (tunnel state + session/job counts), with width-aware truncation that shrinks the status block before shrinking the tabs.

nodes.name: src/tui/ui/config.rs
nodes.summary: Config-tab renderers: a left list of editable keys with selection highlight, a right detail pane showing key/hint/value plus an env-override warning when a VB_* variable outranks config.toml, and a shortcuts hint panel.

nodes.name: src/tui/ui/content.rs
nodes.summary: Content router for the three tabs — splits the area into nav (26 cols) + detail (60/40 vertical) and delegates to sessions/jobs/config renderers based on the active Tab.

nodes.name: src/tui/ui/footer.rs
nodes.summary: Single-row footer: optional status toast (color-coded by Info/Ok/Warn/Err) followed by the persistent keymap cheatsheet (j/k nav, Tab switch, r refresh, l log, ? help, q quit).

nodes.name: src/tui/ui/jobs.rs
nodes.summary: Jobs-tab renderers: list with spinner glyphs for running jobs and ✓/✗/⊘ for terminal statuses, detail pane (id/status/created/finished/error), and a running/completed/failed summary block.

nodes.name: src/tui/ui/mod.rs
nodes.summary: Top-level TUI draw fn — splits the frame into header/content/footer rows and invokes the chrome/content/footer renderers, layering the overlay on top when one is active.

nodes.name: src/tui/ui/overlay/confirm.rs
nodes.summary: Confirmation dialog renderer: centered compact rectangle with the wrapped message and a y/Enter=confirm · n/Esc=cancel hint line.

nodes.name: src/tui/ui/overlay/form.rs
nodes.summary: Config-field editor overlay: 64×9 centered box showing key/hint and a single-line input with a styled cursor (REVERSED in no-color, accent bg otherwise) plus Enter/Esc/arrow hints.

nodes.name: src/tui/ui/overlay/help.rs
nodes.summary: Static help-overlay renderer: 56×18 centered table of global key bindings and tab-specific shortcuts sourced from kv_line.

nodes.name: src/tui/ui/overlay/layout.rs
nodes.summary: Overlay geometry helpers — centered_rect / centered_rect_fixed, content-sized compact_message_overlay_rect, and Unicode-width-aware word wrap (CJK counted as 2 cols); covered by unit tests for ASCII, newlines, and CJK.

nodes.name: src/tui/ui/overlay/log.rs
nodes.summary: Command-log overlay renderer: 85% centered viewport showing a scrollable slice of the command log with per-line color (SKILL=primary, error/error=error, else dim).

nodes.name: src/tui/ui/overlay/mod.rs
nodes.summary: Overlay submodule root — declares the confirm/form/help/layout/log/render submodules.

nodes.name: src/tui/ui/overlay/render.rs
nodes.summary: Single dispatcher that selects confirm/form/help/log rendering based on the active Overlay variant.

nodes.name: src/tui/ui/sessions.rs
nodes.summary: Sessions-tab renderers: list with green-dot glyphs, detail pane (id/port/PID/host/created + optional daemon calls/errors/uptime), and a tunnel-state panel (active vs local mode).

nodes.name: src/tui/ui/shared.rs
nodes.summary: Shared style helpers used by every pane: selection/active-chip/inactive-chip/border styles, kv_line renderer, and Unicode-width-aware truncation for tight layouts.

nodes.name: error.rs
nodes.summary: Defines VirtuosoError, the project-wide error enum, plus CliError helpers. Provides exit_code, error_type, retryable, suggestion, diagnostic_context, and to_cli_error conversion. Implemented via thiserror for ergonomic Display/Error derives.

nodes.name: config_file.rs
nodes.summary: Strongly-typed TOML config file abstraction with key/file/envar resolution, source tracking, schema validation, and atomic save.

nodes.name: models.rs
nodes.summary: Domain models and small helper modules: SkillEvalResult, RpcResponse<T>, VersionInfo, AppPaths (with cache_dir, sessions_dir, load/save), SessionRecord (list/list_remote/sync_from_remote/is_alive), SessionFile helpers, SshBackend, and per-profile config persistence.

nodes.name: src/client/bridge.rs
nodes.summary: VirtuosoClient TCP bridge to the Cadence Virtuoso daemon. Wraps the raw STX/NAK TCP protocol, drives SKILL execution with capability gating and an evalstring whitelist, exposes layout/schematic/maestro/window operation handles, and manages transactions and SSH tunneling.

nodes.name: src/client/editor.rs
nodes.summary: Layout and Schematic editor builder structs (LayoutEditor, SchematicEditor) that collect SKILL commands into a batch and execute them as a single call.

nodes.name: src/client/layout_ops.rs
nodes.summary: LayoutOps SKILL string builder: rodCreateRect, rodCreatePolygon, rodCreatePath, rodCreateVia, rodCreateInstance, xstOutDoTranslate. XstreamOutRequest config struct for tape-out streaming.

nodes.name: src/client/library_ops.rs
nodes.summary: LibraryOps read-only SKILL builder for ddGetLibList(). Tiny unit struct used by the library list command.

nodes.name: src/client/maestro_ops.rs
nodes.summary: MaestroOps builder for SKILL strings driving Cadence Maestro simulation setup (sessions, maeGetSetup, maeSetAnalysis, sweeps, ocean export). ExportWaveformRequest DTO for waveform export.

nodes.name: src/client/mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module index for the client submodule, exporting bridge, editor, layout_ops, library_ops, maestro_ops, schematic_ops, skill_loading (private), skill_runtime (pub(crate)), skill_sexp, symbol_ops, whitelist, window_ops.

nodes.name: src/client/schematic_ops.rs
nodes.summary: SchematicOps SKILL builders for instance creation, wire/instance deletion, property edits, and cellview save/commit. Prepends a cv_guard() that errors when no cellview is open.

nodes.name: src/client/skill_runtime.rs
nodes.summary: Internal helpers for SKILL/JSON interop: escape_string, string_literal, require_identifier, require_transport, require_non_nil, decode_json, decode_json_payload.

nodes.name: src/client/skill_sexp.rs
nodes.summary: S-expression parser for SKILL output. SexpVal enum (Nil/Bool/Str/Atom/List) plus parse_sexp and sexp_to_str_list helpers used to convert daemon responses.

nodes.name: src/client/symbol_ops.rs
nodes.summary: SymbolOps builders for symbol inspection and schSchemToPinList → schPinListToSymbol generation with safe no-overwrite and temp-symbol cleanup.

nodes.name: src/client/whitelist.rs
nodes.summary: evalstring whitelist: blocks dangerous SKILL patterns (system(, sh(, curl, rm -rf, evalstring, etc.) at the CLI before serialization. EvalstringWhitelist supports a sandbox mode that disables evalstring outright.

nodes.name: src/client/window_ops.rs
nodes.summary: WindowOps for window listing and the safe bootstrap interface. BootstrapTarget + BootstrapAction::LoadFile load SKILL programs from a canonicalized scratch dir; raw SKILL execution is forbidden through this path.

nodes.name: src/commands/cell.rs
nodes.summary: CLI command handlers for cell-level operations: open (with mode + dry_run), save, close. Delegates to VirtuosoClient::open_cell_view / save_current_cellview / close_current_cellview.

nodes.name: src/commands/library.rs
nodes.summary: CLI command handler for library list; parses ddGetLibList s-expression output via skill_sexp.

nodes.name: src/commands/maestro.rs
nodes.summary: CLI command handlers for Maestro session control: open/close/list_sessions, set_var, run_analysis, sweep, ocean, and staging guard for ADE windows. StagingGuard ensures window stability before simulation.

nodes.name: src/commands/mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module index for CLI command submodules: cell, config, design, diag, init, library, maestro, process, schema, schematic, session, sim, skill, symbol, transaction, transport_daemon (native-ssh only), tunnel, window.

nodes.name: src/commands/process.rs
nodes.summary: Process corner / DC / AC characterization command handlers (char). Runs Spectre sweeps through the daemon and accumulates data points. OpVals is a small JSON values struct.

nodes.name: src/commands/schema.rs
nodes.summary: Static CLI schema dump for the `vcli schema` introspection command. Hardcodes the full command/flag structure as a serde_json Value.

nodes.name: src/commands/schematic.rs
nodes.summary: CLI command handlers for schematic editing: open/place/wire/delete/property/save. Defines the Orient (R0/R90/.../MYR90) value enum and a YAML-style SchematicSpec parser.

nodes.name: src/commands/symbol.rs
nodes.summary: CLI command handlers for symbol inspection (from SKILL s-expression JSON) and generation (delegates to SymbolOps::generate).

nodes.name: src/commands/transaction.rs
nodes.summary: CLI command handlers for Virtuoso transactions: begin, commit, rollback, diff, status. Thin wrappers around VirtuosoClient::tx_* methods.

nodes.name: src/version.rs
nodes.summary: VirtuosoVersion enum (IC23/IC25/Unknown) and detect_version() that probes the daemon via getVersion(t) and parse_ic_version().

nodes.name: async_runtime.rs
nodes.summary: Thin wrappers around tokio runtime creation (single-threaded and multi-threaded) plus a block_on helper for synchronous bridges.

nodes.name: auth.rs
nodes.summary: Authentication and audit subsystem: API-key init, capability gating, constant-time key comparison, and append-only audit log writer.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Capability model: per-domain capabilities, sets loaded from environment, and a domain-aware permit API with plugin-aware fallthrough.

nodes.name: plugin.rs
nodes.summary: Capability plugin runtime: rate limiting (token bucket), CIDR/IP matching, capability definitions, persisted plugin config and TTL/revoke helpers.

nodes.name: command_log.rs
nodes.summary: Two-line helper module exposing a resolved log path and a synchronous command-log writer used by startup and dispatch.

nodes.name: init.rs
nodes.summary: Project initialization command: scaffolds config, directories and skill discovery into a fresh workspace.

nodes.name: exit_codes.rs
nodes.summary: Process exit-code constants used across binaries for consistent CLI error reporting.

nodes.name: history.rs
nodes.summary: JSONL-backed history of skill invocations and CLI commands with append, tail and load helpers under an inter-process lock.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Library crate root that re-exports the full module tree for binary and integration-test consumers.

nodes.name: main.rs
nodes.summary: CLI entry point and clap-derived command surface: top-level dispatch, key=value parsing, and per-command routers for tunnel, config, profile, target, skill, simulation, schematic, window and RPC commands.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: MCP protocol data model and server struct: request/response/error envelopes plus a request dispatch loop over registered tools.

nodes.name: server.rs
nodes.summary: stdio-line MCP server bootstrap that runs the protocol loop on stdin/stdout.

nodes.name: tools.rs
nodes.summary: MCP tool registry covering schematic, maestro, window, cell, transaction, file, util and skill families with capability-aware filtering.

nodes.name: corner.rs
nodes.summary: Compact data model for Ocean corner/analysis runs: corner config, design target, analysis config, corner set, and measure structs.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Ocean (Spectre/MAESTRO) corner and sweep skill builders plus a small parser for skill list/parameter syntax.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Plugins module root re-exporting registry and schema submodules.

nodes.name: registry.rs
nodes.summary: Plugin registry: on-disk discovery, per-plugin dispatch, MCP tool enumeration, and schema method exposure.

nodes.name: schema.rs
nodes.summary: Plugin schema model with parameter definitions, JSON Schema emission, and skill-bridge helpers to expose plugin methods to the Skill API.

nodes.name: skill_loading.rs
nodes.summary: Helper that stages a local SKILL file on the remote host over the SSH transport before invocation. Copies the local file into a remote temp directory via tempfile + run_command, then executes it through CommandRequest::untimed and validates the response.

nodes.name: config.rs
nodes.summary: CLI subcommand for inspecting the resolved configuration. Implements `check`, an entries JSON dump, source-label resolution, per-entry status reporting, and a tabular renderer; consumed by the `config` subcommand of the vcli binary.

nodes.name: design.rs
nodes.summary: Device-sizing command providing MOSFET `size`, `explore`, and gm/Id lookup-table helpers. Builds lookup tables from raw arrays, finds the closest L for a target gm/Id, and interpolates current density; used during analog sizing flows.

nodes.name: diag.rs
nodes.summary: Diagnostics subcommands including `cdslck` (library lock inspector) and `batch_read_locks` (batched read of cdslck records). Includes shell-quoting, owner-record parsing, age formatting, and a parallel SSH fan-out path over the client bridge.

nodes.name: session.rs
nodes.summary: Largest CLI module: orchestrates session discovery, listing, current-selection, history, cleanup, and detailed show output. Handles local-direct vs remote-tunnel endpoint resolution, hostname/IP matching, version-skew detection, cross-user validation, and TCP reachability checks across the client bridge and transport tunnel.

nodes.name: sim.rs
nodes.summary: Simulation command surface: setup, run, validate_measure_expr, measure, sweep, corner, results, create_netlist, async/parallel job dispatch, job_status/list/cancel, and license check. Calls the spectre jobs/runner and ocean/corner modules for netlist composition, measure-expression validation, and worker pool scheduling.

nodes.name: skill.rs
nodes.summary: SKILL command surface for the vcli binary: exec, broadcast, load, eval, find, info, plus skill_finder directory discovery, remote skill_finder sync, and cache show. Wires SkillFinder paths from the local filesystem or remote skill_runtime through the client bridge.

nodes.name: transport_daemon.rs
nodes.summary: Subcommand entrypoints for the optional `virtuoso-daemon` binary (feature-gated). Provides `run`, `run_with`, and a transport-to-VirtuosoError converter. Backed by transport pool/scheduler/contract modules for Unix-socket daemon management.

nodes.name: tunnel.rs
nodes.summary: SSH tunnel lifecycle management: start, scoped session attach, attach candidate discovery, live session discovery, attach/stop/detach/restart, diagnose, status, backend diagnostics, run, JSON serialization, and PID cleanup helpers. Coordinates transport tunnel/session discovery modules with the client bridge.

nodes.name: window.rs
nodes.summary: GUI window/dialog command surface: list, dismiss_dialog, x11 enumeration and dismissal, screenshot, action_x11/action_x11_batch execution, mode classification, Skill octal escape decoding, and JSON parsing helpers. Provides mode-annotation utilities consumed by the TUI.

nodes.name: config.rs
nodes.summary: Core configuration module: defines ResolvedConfig, ConfigReport, ValueSource, and ConfigValue helpers. Implements env-with-profile resolution, target-based resolution, SSH target derivation, profile selection, digest hashing, build_report generation, and a large set of typed accessor/report methods. Central to the CLI’s config model.

nodes.name: context.rs
nodes.summary: Runtime context that bundles a ResolvedConfig with a target id and exposes ownership validators. Owns config_digest, target_id, and validates session/tunnel/endpoint ownership so commands can refuse actions targeting other users’ resources.

nodes.name: output.rs
nodes.summary: CLI output formatting helpers: resolve format choice, print JSON or human-readable text, print_json, and print_value. Acts as the sink layer between commands and stdout.

nodes.name: dispatcher.rs
nodes.summary: RPC dispatcher routing JSON-RPC method names to specialized handlers: dispatch_schematic, dispatch_maestro, dispatch_window, dispatch_cell, dispatch_tx, dispatch_file, dispatch_util, dispatch_skill, and dispatch_sim. Includes Skill result parsing, octal-escape normalization, and JSON-field coercion helpers.

nodes.name: heartbeat.rs
nodes.summary: Heartbeat watchdog: track active sessions, periodically mark stale ones, and clear stale entries. Used by the daemon/bridge to detect dead SSH sessions and trigger cleanup.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module declaration file for the `session` submodule. Re-exports heartbeat and any sibling modules (currently only heartbeat) and provides no behavior of its own.

nodes.name: parsers.rs
nodes.summary: Spectre PSF output parsers: parse_psf_ascii, parse_psf_dir, parse_psf_signal_file, parse_sweep_psf_directory, strict variants, sweep-flat parser, structured op-block parser, scalar/vector/frequency accessors, and exact-result-file discovery. Implements both lenient and strict PSF formats used by the sim command’s results phase.

nodes.name: profile.rs
nodes.summary: Profile (Virtuoso environment) resolution and binding across venv, user, and local scopes. Resolves profile from explicit flag / env var / venv / user config, and binds/clears it for child processes. Defines ProfileResolution, BindScope.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module root for the typed RPC layer. Declares `dispatcher` and `schema` submodules; replaces raw SKILL strings with `{method, params}` calls that map to SKILL expressions and return typed JSON.

nodes.name: schema.rs
nodes.summary: RPC schema definitions: Method/Param/RpcSchema structs plus standard_schema() returning all built-in RPC methods (schematic, library, design, simulation, etc.) with JSON-Schema-like metadata. Drives discoverable, type-safe API for AI agents.

nodes.name: runtime_paths.rs
nodes.summary: Centralized filesystem path resolution for the bridge runtime. Honours VB_CACHE_DIR / VB_LOG_DIR / VB_HOME / XDG_CACHE_HOME env vars, falls back to dirs::cache_dir(), and provides a legacy_cache_file API for pre-refactor state files.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: SKILL Finder client — query Cadence SKILL API docs from .fnd databases. Supports Fuzzy/Prefix/Suffix/Exact/Regex search modes, remote-host cache (~/.cache/virtuoso_bridge/skill_finder/<host>/), lazy sync, and refresh.

nodes.name: parser.rs
nodes.summary: Hand-rolled state-machine parser for Cadence .fnd SKILL Finder database files. Yields SkillEntry triples (name, syntax, description) tolerant of comments and trailing fields.

nodes.name: maestro_csv.rs
nodes.summary: Parser for Cadence Maestro "Detail" CSV exports (maeExportOutputView). Produces MaestroResult/Point/Output structs with sweep parameters and per-point measurement data, including optional raw_csv passthrough.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module root for Spectre-related types. Aggregates jobs, maestro_csv, parsers, runner submodules.

nodes.name: job_progress.rs
nodes.summary: JobProgressTracker — polls a Spectre spectre.out log, parses progress lines (iteration count, time point), and emits JobEvent::Progress via a JobEventSink. Backs the streaming progress UI.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Streaming event primitives. Defines JobEvent (Started/Progress/Completed/Failed/Cancelled tagged enum), JobEventSink trait, StdoutSink/ChannelSink impls, and helpers for fan-out / throttling.

nodes.name: linux_rename.rs
nodes.summary: Cross-glibc wrapper for renameat2(..., RENAME_NOREPLACE). Tries dlsym, then raw SYS_renameat2 syscall, then a non-atomic lstat + renameat fallback for CentOS 7 / glibc 2.17.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module root for platform compatibility shims. Currently exposes linux_rename on Linux only.

nodes.name: test_env.rs
nodes.summary: Sentinel module documenting that env-mutating tests must use #[serial] from serial_test. Empty body, exists only to give future env-aware test helpers an obvious home.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Top-level in-module test suite for vcli. Configures Config / SSHRunner / SessionInfo, runs SSH command-construction tests, env-var validation, and JSON round-trips. No network or Virtuoso required.

nodes.name: diff.rs
nodes.summary: SchematicDiff: structured diff between two SchematicSnapshots. Tracks instances added/removed/modified, nets added/removed, and pins added/removed with per-parameter old/new values.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Transaction system facade: Transaction / TransactionManager lifecycle over a single VirtuosoClient. Tracks the active tx plus committed history and supports begin/commit/rollback semantics.

nodes.name: snapshot.rs
nodes.summary: SchematicSnapshot: point-in-time capture of a cellview (lib/cell/view + instances, nets, pins, terminal connectivity). Round-trips through serde for diffing and persistence.

nodes.summary: vtui binary entrypoint. Declares all library modules and re-exports the public surface (Capability/Set, standard_schema, SchematicDiff/Snapshot, TransactionManager); calls tui::run_tui() from main.

nodes.name: gui_runner.py
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for the virtuoso-gui-debug skill. Parses arguments, validates scenarios, dispatches FakeExecutor / LiveExecutor / LocalExecutor, and emits exactly one compact JSON object per invocation (with structured exit codes 0/1/2).

nodes.name: command_runner.py
nodes.summary: Fixed-argv subprocess transport for the live executor. Defines CommandError, CommandResult, CommandRunner base class, plus LocalRunner (subprocess.run with cleaned env) and SshRunner (safe shlex.quote of a fixed vcli argv). Rejects shell strings, NUL, newlines, and any remote argv injection.

nodes.name: engine.py
nodes.summary: State machine and step runner for scenario execution. Defines RunState / StepPhase / StepOutcome enums, the Executor ABC, FakeExecutor (deterministic offline outcomes keyed by step/phase/attempt), and the Runner that drives precheck → baseline → execute → verify → recover with retries and JSONL tracing.

nodes.name: live_executor.py
nodes.summary: Real vcli/SSH/X11 executor implementing the Executor protocol against an injected command runner. Binds session/PID/DISPLAY/window at precheck, holds a per-DISPLAY flock, dispatches GUI actions via fixed `vcli window action-x11` argv, sanitizes typed input out of errors, and supports a fast --direct path plus action-x11-batch.

nodes.name: local_executor.py
nodes.summary: Direct xdotool executor for scenarios whose DISPLAY is local to the runner. Implements the Executor protocol via xdotool (search/getwindowgeometry/click/type/key) and ImageMagick import for screenshots. Supports SCROLL (xdotool buttons 4/5/6/7) and binds target window by PID at precheck.

nodes.name: model.py
nodes.summary: Strict scenario parser producing deeply immutable dataclasses (Scenario, Step, CellView) with the Operation enum, per-operation argument schemas, integer/string/predicate allowlists, and ScenarioValidationError on any deviation. Supports version 1.0 round-trip via MappingProxyType.

nodes.name: trace.py

nodes.name: daemon.rs
nodes.summary: Synchronous `NativeTransportClient` (Unix-only) that talks the versioned IPC protocol to the transport daemon. Implements `RemoteTransport` over a length-prefixed JSON frame channel on a Unix domain socket: performs the `Hello` handshake (profile, auth token, daemon nonce), then offers test_connection / run_command / upload_file|upload_text / download_file|download_dir / challenge / request_shutdown. Also owns the end-to-end integration `mod tests` that round-trips through the real server.

nodes.name: framing.rs
nodes.summary: Transport-agnostic byte framing for the IPC protocol: four-byte big-endian length prefix + UTF-8 payload, with an 8 MiB hard ceiling (`MAX_FRAME_SIZE`). Exposes `encode_frame`, `FrameReader<R: Read>` (streaming, deadline-aware `read_frame_until`/`read_frame_until_with`), and `FrameWriter<W: Write>` (`write_frame_with_deadline`). `FrameError` covers TooLarge, Truncated, and Io variants. The layer never sees SSH, Tokio, or daemon-internal types.

nodes.name: messages.rs
nodes.summary: Plain `serde` request/response vocabulary for the IPC protocol: `ProtocolVersion` (major/minor, current constants pulled from `framing`, major must match exactly), `Operation` enum (Hello, RunCommand, UploadFile, DownloadDir, Health, Shutdown, etc., with custom serde via `as_str`), `Hello`/`HelloAck`, `RequestEnvelope`/`ResponseEnvelope`/`ResponseResult`, and the `IpcError` taxonomy (codes, connection-level predicate, and From impls for serde_json / std::io errors).

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module root for `transport::ipc`. Declares `daemon`, `framing`, `messages`, and `server` submodules, with `daemon`/`server` gated on `(unix, any(test, feature = "native-ssh"))` because the real daemon is feature-gated but the test suite exercises the same code. The module owns only the wire format; no russh, Tokio, SSH, or daemon-internal types leak.

nodes.name: server.rs
nodes.summary: Server half of the versioned IPC protocol (Unix-only). `serve_one` / `serve_one_with_shutdown` handle a single connection: `Hello` handshake, then dispatch every subsequent `RequestEnvelope` onto the supplied `RemoteTransport` (or an `EndpointPool` via `serve_one_pooled`/`run_with_pool`) until the peer closes. `dispatch` is the central request router (~130 lines, handles RunCommand, uploads, downloads, Health, Shutdown, Challenge, Cancel, local-forward). `run` binds the Unix socket, sets mode `0600`, and accepts forever. Implements the Tier-1 liveness `Challenge` probe by answering with the recorded daemon nonce.

nodes.name: probe_signatures.py
nodes.summary: Reverse-engineers SKILL function argument counts by invoking each known function with 0..5 nil arguments and parsing the error message to recover the expected arity and a cleaned signature string. Wraps a per-function probe (probe_signature) and a batch driver (run_signature_probe) that reads the candidate list from skill_db.get_known_functions, threads Popen subprocess calls with a short timeout, and stores results back via skill_db.record_function.

nodes.name: skill_db.py

nodes.name: enumerate_functions.py

nodes.name: probe_signatures.py

The aggregated probe results are then written back as a compact signature string per function.

nodes.name: ci.yml (CI workflow)
nodes.summary: Primary CI workflow for the Rust workspace. Triggers on push and PR to main. Runs four jobs sequentially-on-same-runner (each independent runner, no needs): (1) check — fmt --check + clippy with -D warnings across default, --features daemon, and --features native-ssh; (2) test — cargo test on default features; (3) build — cargo build for default and --features daemon; (4) audit — pinned cargo-audit 0.22.2 with --ignore RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (Marvin RSA timing side-channel, reachable only via ssh-key->russh under native-ssh; full rationale in audit.toml). Uses actions/checkout@v7, dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable (with clippy, rustfmt for check), and Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 on every job. CARGO_TERM_COLOR=always. 59 lines / 4 jobs.

nodes.name: integration.yml (Integration Matrix)

The header comment explicitly states the goal: catch Windows-only native build breaks here rather than at release time, and avoid one OS masking another via fail-fast:false. 34 lines / 1 matrix job / 6 effective jobs.

nodes.name: release.yml (Release workflow)
nodes.summary: Tag-driven release workflow that builds, packages, and uploads binaries plus optionally publishes to crates.io. Triggers on push of v* tags. Five jobs with explicit needs: (1) build-linux-x86_64 — ubuntu-latest, builds vcli/vtui with --features native-ssh and virtuoso-daemon with --features daemon, packages as `dist/{vcli,vtui,virtuoso-daemon}-${TAG}-linux-x86_64`, uploads via softprops/action-gh-release@v3 with auto-generated notes pointing to CHANGELOG.md; (2) build-linux-aarch64 — ubuntu-latest with aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu target, installs gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu, patches ~/.cargo/config.toml with the linker, daemon-only build, uploads daemon only; (3) build-macos-aarch64 — macos-latest (Apple Silicon), same triple-binary packaging; (4) build-windows-x86_64 — windows-latest with shell:bash for packaging, .exe suffix; (5) publish-crate — gated on all four builds, uses CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN secret, idempotent (skips silently if token unset or version already published). permissions: contents: write. 159 lines / 5 jobs.

nodes.name: security-audit.yml (Security audit)
nodes.summary: Dedicated dependency vulnerability scan that surfaces RUSTSEC advisories on every dependency change and weekly. Path-triggered on **/Cargo.toml, **/Cargo.lock, audit.toml, and the workflow file itself; scheduled Monday ~03:37 UTC (off-peak to avoid the :00 stampede); also runnable via workflow_dispatch. Header comment explains why this workflow deliberately does NOT use rustsec/audit-check@v2.0.0 (that wrapper compiles cargo-audit from source and currently fails with 'Couldn't load ./Cargo.lock' because it runs outside the repo root) and instead installs a pinned cargo-audit 0.22.2 --locked directly and runs it from the repo root. Single audit job with the same RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (rsa Marvin) ignore as ci.yml, this time enforced on the command line because cargo-audit 0.22.2 does not auto-read audit.toml. permissions: contents: read, checks: write. 50 lines / 1 job.

nodes.name: skill-tests.yml (Skill Tests)

nodes.summary: Concise project guide for Claude Code: mandates use of the .claude/skills/virtuoso-gui-debug skill for Virtuoso window operations, X11 automation, and GUI regression testing. Documents three executor modes (fake/live/local), the validate→run→inspect workflow, the supported scenario DSL ops (VCLI_LOAD, WINDOW_WAIT, KEY, CLICK_REL, DRAG_REL, SCROLL, SCREENSHOT, VERIFY, RECOVER), and pointers to the scenario schema, xdotool cheatsheet, and unit tests.

nodes.name: .claude/settings.json
nodes.summary: Shared Claude Code settings defining PostToolUse hooks. Write|Edit tools trigger .claude/hooks/rust_check.sh to lint/format Rust; Bash commands trigger .claude/hooks/auto_plot.sh and .claude/hooks/eda_error_capture.sh to process plot output and capture EDA stderr. Paths are resolved via $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR.

nodes.name: .claude/settings.local.json
nodes.summary: Local-machine Claude Code permissions override, allowing the Bash tool to invoke `gh run:*` (GitHub Actions run inspection) without prompting.

nodes.name: auto_plot.sh
nodes.summary: Claude Code PostToolUse hook that auto-plots simulation results. Reads a hook JSON payload from stdin, filters for `vcli sim sweep|measure` or `virtuoso sim sweep|measure` or `process char` commands with `--format json`, then invokes the Python helper `.claude/skills/sim-plot/scripts/plot_sim.py` to render a chart (line, bar, or gm/Id lookup) into `plots/<prefix>_<timestamp>.png`. Selects a plot prefix (`sweep` / `measure` / `gmid`) from the command verb, silently bails when jq/python3 are missing or JSON output is empty/unparsable, and returns a `systemMessage` via jq pointing to the saved PNG. Failures from plot_sim.py are deliberately swallowed.

nodes.name: eda_error_capture.sh
nodes.summary: Claude Code PostToolUse hook that classifies EDA errors emitted by `vcli`, `virtuoso`, or `spectre` Bash invocations and saves them into per-skill `memory/` files via `.claude/skills/_shared/scripts/eda_memory_saver.py`. Reads the hook JSON from stdin, pre-filters the tool response with a regex covering SFE-/OSSHNL- codes, premature termination, IPC failures, bridge NAK, missing skill registration, nil netlists, connection refused, and exit 127; classifies the source as `spectre`/`vcli`/`unknown`; pipes the output through the saver; and surfaces a localized `systemMessage` (`[eda_capture] 已记录到 <skill>/memory/: <pattern>`) on success.

nodes.name: rust_check.sh
nodes.summary: Claude Code PostToolUse hook that auto-formats and lints Rust files after Write/Edit. Reads the hook JSON, validates that `tool_input.file_path` ends with `.rs` and lives under `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, then runs `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check` before and after `cargo fmt --quiet` to detect whether formatting was applied (emitting a systemMessage only on a before→after transition). If the file is formatted, runs `cargo clippy -q -- -D warnings`, extracts the first ten `error...` lines and up to five `= help:` hints, and surfaces them as a single systemMessage naming the file. Silently exits if rustfmt/jq are missing.

nodes.name: _shared README

nodes.name: vcli ↔ virtuoso naming convention
nodes.summary: Single source of truth for the `vcli` (binary) vs `virtuoso` (documented name) convention used by 16 of 27 SKILL.md files. Covers: TL;DR mapping table, why the corpus uses `virtuoso` (collision with the Cadence GUI executable, documentation drift), how the vcli.sh adapter resolves the binary (VCLI_BIN override → ~/.cargo/bin/vcli → ./target/release/vcli → PATH → /opt/cargo/bin/vcli) and forwards argv unchanged, one-time install recipe, the single-point migration contract (only vcli.sh + convention.md change when the binary is renamed), SKILL.md hygiene rules (use `virtuoso` in examples; allowed-tools globs), an extensive diagnostic playbook with 13 H3-level rules covering disk-cache silent writes, ramic_bridge.il one-shot load, Admin-gated RPC pool split, snake_case RPC naming, Maestro write split, IC25 SKILL string-quoted kwargs, ADE Editing-mode `mae*` session resolution, bypass-mode maestro.run disk-only writes, IC25 compressed PSF, session-close ownership, ?session + ~>name rejection, VB_REMOTE_HOST requirements for create_corner_netlist, and Cadence-version citation hygiene, plus a maintenance contract describing when to edit and when not to.

nodes.name: vcli.sh wrapper
nodes.summary: Bash adapter that bridges the `virtuoso` documented name to the actual `vcli` Rust binary. Performs five roles: identity (accepts both names via $0 basename, forwards argv unchanged), binary resolution (VCLI_BIN override → ~/.cargo/bin/vcli → ./target/release/vcli → command -v vcli → /opt/cargo/bin/vcli, with PATH-ordering rationale documented inline), stderr logging (duplicates into $VB_LOG_DIR/harness-YYYYMMDD.log so forensic traces survive the harness's stdout buffer TTL), environment defaults (sets VB_TIMEOUT=120 if unset), and doctor subcommand diagnostics. Execs the resolved binary so its exit code reaches the harness unmodified. Does NOT rewrite argv, inject --format json, retry, or swallow errors.

nodes.name: Batch Netlist (si)
nodes.summary: Reference for generating Spectre/HSPICE netlists with Cadence's `si` batch translator instead of Maestro. Documents generating si.env via `simInitEnvWithArgs`, the si.env field schema (simLibName, simCellName, simViewName, simSimulator, simViewList, simStopList, simNetlistHier, nlDesignVarNameList), invoking `si -batch -command nl` via the bridge shell runner, the Spectre vs HSPICE flag difference (`-command nl` vs `-command netlist`), and contrasts `si` netlisting with `maeCreateNetlistForCorner` (no resolved params, no model include, no sim commands, no Maestro dependency). Includes viewing the resulting netlist via `(view path)` and the alternative `maeCreateNetlistForCorner` path.

nodes.name: Layout Python API

nodes.name: Maestro Python API
nodes.summary: Python wrapper (`virtuoso_bridge.virtuoso.maestro`) for Cadence Maestro (ADE Assembler) SKILL functions. nodes.name: Maestro SKILL API Reference
nodes.summary: Comprehensive low-level SKILL reference for Cadence Maestro/ADE Assembler. Covers session modes (background vs GUI) with a comparison table, the full `mae*` API surface for IC618/IC231 (session management, reading setup, creating tests, analysis configuration with backtick-quoted options, outputs and specs, design variables, corners including `maeSetVar`+`axl*` pure-SKILL setup and the legacy `maestro.sdb` XML editing fallback, environment options, save, run with `?callback` and blocking-wait caveats, programmatic result reading), `asi*` fallback table for older Virtuoso (with `fboundp` runtime detection), known blockers (GUI dialogs, schematic check, edit locks), the pnoise jitter event automation limitation (what works via `maeSetAnalysis`/`asiSetAnalysisFieldVal`, what does NOT work, the `active.state` XML copy+sed workaround, explored-and-failed approaches table), the OCEAN result-reading API, a complete end-to-end Maestro workflow example, and the `axl*` setup-DB API for variable management (deleting test-level/global variables that `maeDeleteVar` cannot reach).

nodes.name: Netlist Reference
nodes.summary: Reference for netlist formats (CDL/SPICE vs Cadence Spectre), parameter and source-device mapping, and the import/export round-trip. Documents CDL syntax (`.SUBCKT`, `Xname`, bus notation `BOT<3:0>`), Spectre syntax (`subckt (pins)`, escaped buses `BOT\<0\>`, full device names `capacitor`), a key-differences table (pin syntax, device names, bus escaping, parameter case), schematic-CDF vs netlist parameter mapping (`acm`→`mag`, `vdc`→`dc`), the analogLib `vsin` → Spectre `vsource type=sine` source device mapping, CDL → Virtuoso schematic import via `spiceIn` (must run via SSH, requires devmap.txt, `schPinListToSymbol` for auto-generated symbols), Virtuoso → Spectre netlist export via `maeCreateNetlistForCorner` with a temp Maestro view, direct SKILL schematic connectivity reads (`cv~>instances`, `inst~>instTerms`, `net~>name`, `cv~>terminals`), the full round-trip pipeline, and sample netlists in `references/netlist_samples/` (rc_cascade 2-stage RC low-pass, AC-verified 2-pole roll-off at 159 MHz).

nodes.name: Schematic Python API
nodes.summary: Python wrapper (`virtuoso_bridge.virtuoso.schematic`) for Cadence Virtuoso schematic editing via SKILL. Documents the `SchematicEditor` context manager (queues ops, runs `schCheck` + `dbSave` on `__exit__`), `SchematicEditor` methods (`add`, `add_net_label_to_transistor`), SKILL builder ops (`schematic_create_inst_by_master_name`, `schematic_create_wire`, `schematic_create_wire_label`, `schematic_create_pin`, `schematic_create_pin_at_instance_term`, `schematic_create_wire_between_instance_terms`, `schematic_label_instance_term`), the immediate-execution `SchematicOps` class (`open`, `save`, `check`, `add_instance`, `add_wire`, `add_label`, `add_pin`, `add_pin_to_instance_term`, `add_wire_between_instance_terms`, `add_net_label_to_instance_term`, `add_net_label_to_transistor`), low-level SKILL string builders in `schematic/ops.py`, and terminal-aware helpers (MOS D/G/S/B auto-direction for the transistor label helper).

nodes.name: Recreate a Schematic from an Existing Design
nodes.summary: Workflow for reading an existing schematic, mapping instances to a uniform grid, and redrawing cleanly with net stubs. Three steps: (1) read original via `virtuoso_bridge.virtuoso.schematic.reader.read_schematic(client, LIB, CELL, include_positions=True)`, (2) map to grid — sort by y for rows, sort by x within row for columns, identify differential pairs (R0 left / MY mirrored right), choose GRID spacing (1.5 recommended), (3) redraw using `client.schematic.edit()` with placement tuples `(name, cell, col, row, orient)` and connectivity labels `(name, drain, gate, source, body)` using `add_net_label_to_transistor`. Key rules: GRID=1.5, NMOS at bottom rows / PMOS at top, pins in dedicated leftmost column (col=-1), output stages offset right (col 5-6), no explicit wires (only labels, same net name = same net), verify with CIW screenshot after every run.

nodes.name: Schematic Reference (SKILL-style patterns)
nodes.summary: Compact recipe-style reference for schematic editing using the Python API wrappers. Covers the `with client.schematic.edit(lib, cell) as sch:` pattern (instance placement, wiring between terminals, term labels, pin creation, MOS D/G/S/B labeling), CDF parameter setting via `set_instance_params` for PDK devices (handles `schHiReplace` + CDF callback) and direct `cdfFindParamByName`/`cdfGetInstCDF` for analogLib devices, and reading placement via `read_placement`. Tips: use `add_net_label_to_transistor` for MOS D/G/S/B, prefer `schematic_label_instance_term` / `schematic_create_wire_between_instance_terms` over guessing coordinates, always `schCheck` + `dbSave` before simulation (otherwise netlisting fails with a blocking dialog), schematic should be open in GUI for Maestro.

nodes.name: Standard Simulation Flow (GUI Mode)
nodes.summary: End-to-end Maestro simulation flow in GUI mode (8 steps: purge stale cellviews, open GUI session, optionally modify vars/outputs, save+run+wait, read results, optionally export waveforms; with an alternate path when a GUI session is already open). Documents how `run_and_wait` works (defines a SKILL `?callback` procedure that writes a marker file, polls via SSH, SKILL channel stays free), how to detect Maestro session state by parsing the window title via `hiGetWindowName` (the only reliable method — `maeIsEditable`/`axlGetSetupMode` return nil), how to close Maestro sessions (`maeCloseSession` won't work for GUI-opened sessions → ASSEMBLER-8051, must use `hiCloseWindow` after `maeSaveSetup`), a common-pitfalls table (ASSEMBLER-8127, wait_until_done immediate return, maeCloseResults read-only switch, `window:N` unbound variable, empty read_results), the optimization loop pattern (sweep param → save → run_and_wait → read), and the manual `maeOpenResults`/`maeGetOutputValue`/`maeCloseResults` fallback when `read_results` returns empty.

nodes.name: Copy a Testbench to Another Library
nodes.summary: Workflow for replicating a testbench + Maestro setup in a new library. Five steps: (1) copy the DUT cell via `dbCopyCellView` (takes a db object, not a string — both schematic and symbol views), (2) create the testbench schematic with `schematic.edit()` + `inst()` + `label_term()`, set source parameters per-instance via `cdfGetInstCDF` (never `schHiReplace` with `cellName` matching — it hits ALL instances), always use `dbOpenCellViewByType` instead of `geGetEditCellView` (window-focus dependent), (3) CDF param name gotchas — table mapping analogLib cells (vsin, vdc, idc, cap) to their CDF params (`vdc`, `va`, `sinephase`, `freq`) vs Spectre netlist params (`sinedc`, `ampl`, `sinephase`, `freq`), (4) create Maestro via `.il` files for `maeSetAnalysis` (Python can't handle backtick + nested quotes reliably), `maeAddOutput` requires unique non-nil names, analysis options must use bare variable names not `VAR("...")` (Maestro runtime, not translated by netlister), (5) run via `deOpenCellView` first (required for `maeRunSimulation`), poll `spectre.out` via SSH (don't trust `maeWaitUntilDone`). Key pitfalls table at the end.

nodes.name: Troubleshooting — Known Gotchas & Pitfalls
nodes.summary: Curated troubleshooting index across five areas: (1) SKILL/CIW — `csh()`/`sh()` return t/nil not output (use `download_file`), `procedurep()` returns nil for compiled functions like `maeCreateNetlistForCorner`, `inst~>prop` returns nil for PDK devices (use `cdfGetInstCDF`), (2) GUI dialog blocking — `simInitEnvWithArgs` triggers 'Run Directory exists' dialog on existing dirs, Maestro dialogs block the SKILL channel (recovery via `hiFormDone`, screenshot via `hiWindowSaveImage`), ASSEMBLER-8127 from `maeMakeEditable()` when cellview already open in another session (deadlock recovery via X11 `XTestFakeKeyEvent` Enter key, prevention via title check), (3) netlist/si — netlist files are on the remote (use `download_file`), si outputs to single `<runDir>/netlist` file, (4) Maestro/design variables — `mae*` undefined fallback to `asi*` (see maestro-skill-api.md), `maeGetSetup(?typeName "globalVar")` returns nil (use `asiGetDesignVarList`), global vs test-level variables (`?typeName "test" ?typeValue '("test")`), must `maeSaveSetup` before `maeRunSimulation`, window title 'Reading' vs 'Editing' diagnosis and fix (close + reopen with `deOpenCellView(... "a")`), stale `.cdslck` lock file fix, the Outputs 'Save' checkbox has NO SKILL API (only manual or `spectre -raw` workarounds), (5) connection/tunnel — 30s socket timeout, `OPEN_FAILED` on locked views, `.il line 16` SKILL probe failure (re-run setup.il).

nodes.name: gui_click.sh
nodes.summary: Shell script that performs a mouse click at absolute screen coordinates via xdotool, with optional mouse-button and click-count selection. Activates the previously locked window (state from gui_find.sh), moves the cursor, clicks, then auto-captures a verify screenshot via ImageMagick `import` and writes a structured line to /tmp/gui_actions.log.

nodes.name: gui_drag.sh
nodes.summary: Shell script that executes a smooth mouse drag between two absolute screen points by interpolating intermediate positions with xdotool mousedown / mousemove / mouseup. Configurable button (left/middle/right) and step count (default 8) for trajectory smoothness. Logs the drag to /tmp/gui_actions.log.

nodes.name: gui_env.sh
nodes.summary: Shell preflight check that verifies the X11 GUI-driver prerequisites: DISPLAY is set, session is not Wayland (xdotool requires X), and the `xdotool` binary exists. Issues a non-fatal warning if neither `import` (ImageMagick) nor `scrot` is installed for the screenshot channel. Reports display geometry via `xdotool getdisplaygeometry`.

nodes.name: gui_find.sh
nodes.summary: Shell script that searches for a visible X11 window by name then class via xdotool, takes the first match, and persists its window id as `GUI_WID` into the shared state file (default /tmp/gui_session.env). All later click/type actions in this session are then window-scoped to that id. Logs the lock event to /tmp/gui_actions.log.

nodes.name: gui_scroll.sh
nodes.summary: Shell script that issues mouse-wheel scroll input at absolute screen coordinates. Maps the symbolic direction `up/down/left/right` onto the corresponding xdotool button codes (4/5/6/7) and emits N repeats with a small delay between clicks. Logs the scroll event to /tmp/gui_actions.log.

nodes.name: gui_shot.sh
nodes.summary: Shell utility that captures the root-window screenshot to a path (default /tmp/gui_shot.png). Prefers ImageMagick `import` (matches xdotool-based workflows) and falls back to `scrot`. Exits non-zero if neither tool is present. Logs the capture to /tmp/gui_actions.log.

nodes.name: gui_state.sh
nodes.summary: Shell introspection helper that lists the first ~40 visible X11 windows (id / truncated name / parsed geometry) and prints the currently active window. Designed to be called during the observation phase of an OODA-style loop so the decision layer can see what is actually on screen.

nodes.name: gui_type.sh
nodes.summary: Shell script that focuses the locked window and types a text string via `xdotool type --clearmodifiers --delay …`. Default per-key delay of 30 ms to avoid dropped characters in the target application. Logs the LENGTH only to /tmp/gui_actions.log so passwords and secrets never reach the audit log.

nodes.name: gui_wait.sh
nodes.summary: Shell polling helper that waits until a window matching a name/class substring becomes visible (`appear` mode, default) or disappears (`disappear` mode). Implements a busy-wait loop with a hard wall-clock timeout (in seconds). Exits 0 when the condition is met, 1 on timeout.

nodes.name: smoke.sh
nodes.summary: Shell orchestrator that runs a 6-stage self-test of the GUI-debug toolkit: env check → launch `xmessage` → find/lock the window → pre-click screenshot → convert window-relative to absolute coordinates and click the OK button → verify the window closed. Prints `SMOKE PASS` on success, `SMOKE FAIL` plus non-zero exit on failure. Skips gracefully if `xmessage` is missing.

nodes.name: auto_plot.sh
nodes.summary: PostToolUse bash hook that auto-generates PNG plots whenever a `vcli sim sweep`, `vcli sim measure`, or `vcli process char` command is invoked with `--format json`. Reads the hook JSON from stdin, filters on command regex and format flag, validates the tool response is parseable JSON, chooses a plot prefix (sweep/measure/gmid), and pipes the response into plot_sim.py to write a timestamped PNG under plots/. Emits a JSON systemMessage with the relative + absolute plot path on success; silently exits on non-matching or unplottable inputs. Top-level logic split: filter_and_validate (lines 13-37), determine_prefix (lines 39-48), run_plotter (lines 50-68).

nodes.name: eda_error_capture.sh
nodes.summary: PostToolUse bash hook that captures EDA tool errors (Spectre SFE-/OSSHNL- codes, IPC failures, bridge NAKs, missing skill registrations, etc.) emitted by `vcli`, `virtuoso`, or `spectre` commands and routes them to eda_memory_saver.py for skill-scoped memory persistence. Reads hook JSON from stdin, pre-filters the tool response for known error fingerprints, classifies the source (spectre/vcli/unknown), then invokes the saver and echoes back a systemMessage that names the destination skill and matched pattern. Sections: filter_command (lines 7-19), pre_filter_errors (lines 21-28), classify_source (lines 30-37), run_saver (lines 39-50).

nodes.name: rust_check.sh
nodes.summary: PostToolUse bash hook that auto-formats and lint-checks Rust source files immediately after a Write/Edit operation. Reads hook JSON from stdin, gates on file extension `.rs` and a $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR path prefix, then runs `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check` before/after a `cargo fmt --quiet` to detect auto-fixes (emitting a systemMessage when a fix was applied). If formatting is clean, it then runs `cargo clippy -q -- -D warnings` and surfaces the first ten errors and five help hints as a systemMessage so the model can react. Sections: gate_input (lines 7-17), run_fmt (lines 19-27), run_clippy (lines 29-41).

nodes.name: Session vs Profile: Two-Layer Connection Addressing
nodes.summary: Decision documenting that Session (auto-registered Virtuoso process identity on a server, selects daemon port) and Profile (manually configured environment via VB_*_<profile> env vars, selects server + connection params) are orthogonal layers composing connection addressing. State files are profile-scoped; sessions are not. Examples: "--profile gpu1 --session eda-meow-3" targets the 3rd Virtuoso on the gpu1 server.

nodes.name: TODO: createNetlist 路径 CMI-2116 问题
nodes.summary: Open TODO documenting that for SMIC 0.13µm mmRF PDK (n33/p33 BSIM3v3), all Cadence netlist export paths omit MOSFET port connections (CMI-2116) because port mapping lives in the OA binary DB and spectre must query it at runtime via -env ade +adespetkn=TOKEN. Lists paths already verified to fail on 2026-04-19 (Ocean createNetlist, virtuoso-daemon convertNetlist, ADE GUI netlist). Documents current workaround and investigation directions. Update 2026-04-20 adds that all IC23.1 Maestro APIs that trigger netlisting block the bridge.

nodes.name: LLM-Assisted Inline Repair for Intermittent Netlist Issues
nodes.summary: Decision to use an LLM (instead of bespoke patch scripts) to read and fix intermittent netlist structural defects — e.g., rhrpo_3t_ckt resistors with 0 terminals, MOSFET instances missing (D G S B), BJTs missing (C B E). Driven by PDK-version/schematic-version variability. Justification: low frequency, structurally diverse, often new — script maintenance cost exceeds LLM call cost. Includes a prompt template with verification steps (model-file lookup, terminal-order discovery, subckt re-emission).

nodes.name: Standalone Spectre for One-Off Circuit Verification
nodes.summary: Decision to extract OA topology via SKILL (dbOpenCellViewByType + dbTraverseElements) and emit a topology-complete input.scs for standalone Spectre, instead of fighting ADE token / Maestro paths. Used for FT0001A_SH/CMOP/schematic (static comparator) — supports DC op, DC sweep, transient. Alternatives considered and rejected: ADE netlist (CMI-2116), -env ade +adespetkn=TOKEN (stale token), maeRunSimulation (modal blocks bridge 30s). Includes a SKILL topology-extraction template.

nodes.name: virtuoso-bridge-lite 借鉴范围决策
nodes.summary: Selective port decision from Arcadia-1/virtuoso-bridge-lite. Adopts (a) Callback File IPC into ramic_bridge.il + src/daemon/main.rs to fix IC23.1/RHEL8 second-call hang, and (b) vcli maestro session-info for atomically exposing current ADE design as structured JSON. Defers variable scope/sweep (no current need; maeSetVar suffices) and SanitizingClient (existing escape_skill_string already secure). nodes.name: SKILL nil return is not a transport error

nodes.name: aarch64 Cross-Compile Setup

nodes.name: Architecture Review 2026-07-13 — virtuoso-bridge-lite

nodes.name: Simulation Automation Module Design
nodes.summary: Design doc for a new `virtuoso sim` command subtree that automates ADE-L analog simulation by generating Ocean SKILL and dispatching it through the existing SKILL bridge. Defines the command tree (setup, run, sweep, corner, measure, results), typical workflows (single sim, parameter sweep, PVT corner analysis), a corner configuration file format, an Ocean SKILL generation architecture, error handling strategy, output format, and environment verification. Targets Cadence IC23.1 with Ocean API functions (simulator, design, analysis, run, openResults, getData, value, cross, ymax, ymin).

nodes.name: Bayesian Optimization Skill for Circuit Auto-Tuning
nodes.summary: Approved design for a closed-loop Bayesian circuit auto-tuner implemented as a virtuoso-cli skill. Uses Claude itself as the surrogate (no external Python/ML deps), gm/Id + L as the parameter space, a hierarchical scoring function (feasibility first, then targets) aligned with spec template min/max/target structure, and a three-phase progressive PVT strategy (TT → FF/SS → temperature). Describes the suggest/simulate/measure/update iteration sequence, stopping criteria, JSON history file, and the catalogue of skill dependencies it composes.

nodes.name: sim run Robustness Fixes
nodes.summary: Task-by-task implementation plan to make `sim run` and `sim measure` detect and report failures instead of returning false success. Adds post-run validation in `src/commands/sim.rs` (verify run() return + spectre.out existence), diagnostic hints for all-nil measure results, a new `sim netlist` subcommand for programmatic netlist regeneration, and a SKILL-command guard for dangerous forms (e.g. exit, shell-out). Front-matter is targeted at Claude with a required sub-skill 'executing-plans'.

nodes.name: Borrow from virtuoso-bridge-lite — Review & Plan

Documents which upstream features have already been adopted (cross-user daemon guard, profile-isolated scratch dirs, SKILL Finder + remote cache, parallel SpectreSimulator, maestro::snapshot, etc.) with adoption commits, then identifies four remaining gaps (X11/dialog deadlock bypass, .cdslck sniffer, knowledge transfer, digital-import edge cases) with concrete specs and an estimated-effort matrix. Also lists features that should NOT be adopted and open questions.

nodes.name: Design: Virtuoso-CLI AI Circuit Optimization Framework
nodes.summary: Builder-mode design doc (generated by /office-hours) framing the AI circuit optimization framework problem: analog designers currently hand-iterate simulate → tweak → re-simulate. Proposes an end-to-end auto-optimization approach that pairs LLM reasoning with gm/Id methodology over a virtuoso-cli Rust daemon + SKILL bridge, with auto pass/fail spec comparison. Wedge: Bandgap IP. Lists constraints, three considered approaches (batch automation, AI-assisted, end-to-end), recommended path, open questions, success criteria, and a distribution plan.

nodes.name: virtuoso-cli AI-First EDA Infrastructure Enhancement Proposal

Catalogues current strengths (session registry + dynamic port, JSON-first CLI, noun-verb structure, Rust choice), diagnoses the structural gap (abstraction layer too low), then lays out a phased roadmap: Phase 1 safety/stability (typed RPC layer, security hardening, MCP support), Phase 2 architecture (EDA object model, design diff engine, transaction/rollback), Phase 3 AI-native (graph-based design representation, simulation job system, TUI → EDA IDE). Closes with Cadence-version compatibility risks and contribution recommendations.

nodes.name: SKILL Runtime Implementation Plan
nodes.summary: TDD implementation plan that centralizes SKILL string-literal escaping, transport/non-nil result semantics, and JSON decoding into a new internal `client::skill_runtime` module. Preserves the existing Rust public Interface and CLI success output while migrating schematic, maestro, ocean, process, and sim call sites.

nodes.name: Upstream Hardening Implementation Plan

Bound by global constraints forbidding new dependencies, CLI commands, env vars, commits, or pushes.

nodes.name: Virtuoso GUI Live Executor Implementation Plan

nodes.name: Virtuoso GUI Runner Foundation Implementation Plan
nodes.summary: Foundation plan for safe, deterministic offline replay of validated Virtuoso GUI-debug scenarios without a live `vcli`/X11/xdotool. Self-review section explicitly defers real `vcli`, SKILL adapter, X11, screenshots, live recovery, and PVT/PDK integration.

nodes.name: SKILL Runtime Refinement Design
nodes.summary: Architecture-spec for centralizing SKILL string-literal escaping, transport/non-nil result semantics, and JSON decoding into a new internal `client::skill_runtime` module sitting between domain commands and `VirtuosoClient::execute_skill()`. Defines four runtime capabilities (string literal, require_transport, require_non_nil, decode_json), a data-flow diagram, migration scope across `src/commands/sim.rs`, `process.rs`, `ocean/mod.rs`, `schematic.rs`, and `maestro.rs`, error-handling rules, TDD test strategy covering runtime unit tests and OCEAN builder regressions, explicit non-goals (no typed SKILL AST, no new CLI commands, no daemon wire changes), and completion criteria requiring a shared decoder/escape path, schematic noun parser removal, and strict Clippy + full test pass.

nodes.name: Native Remote Transport Design
nodes.summary: Comprehensive design for a pure-Rust russh-based SSH transport running as a hidden local `vcli __transport-daemon` mode, layered atop the existing OpenSSH backend and selected explicitly via `VB_SSH_BACKEND=native`. Documents v1.2.0 delivered status with explicit deltas (SOCKS5/ProxyJump and RAMIC/X11 forwarding deferred), terminology distinguishing transport daemon from `virtuoso-daemon`, `RemoteTransport` trait, `Arc<dyn RemoteTransport>` handoff, connection identity/pooling, channel scheduler with capacity invariant, file transfer via streaming SFTP, reconnect/retry safety, host-key and SSH configuration policy, versioned local IPC protocol with state-file versioning, error model, health/observability, dependency boundary (no Python/Paramiko/libssh2/system SSH), testing topology with contract tests, and delivery sequence table. Calls out Linux/macOS/Windows integration matrices.

nodes.name: Upstream Hardening Design

Validation enumerates test-first acceptance via `cargo test --lib client::maestro_ops`, `cargo test --lib spectre::parsers`, full `cargo test`, strict Clippy, and `cargo fmt --check`.

nodes.name: Virtuoso GUI Real Executor Design

nodes.name: content.md
nodes.summary: Pensieve knowledge note covering ocean design cell switch. Documents that switching target cell in Ocean requires an explicit `design(lib cell view)` call before netlisting: the previous design's desVar() state is per-design, so a fresh session may return nil. nodes.name: content.md

Documents the RAMIC bridge callback-file IPC protocol used to send async callbacks from the SKILL/RAMIC side to the Rust daemon: a platform bug forces file-based IPC instead of TCP; the file must use the actual listening port (not the registration port) for `cb_port`. nodes.name: content.md

The two crates must each declare their own allow attributes — a gotcha when tightening warnings.
